**Triage**

- **Minor (typo "neerest"):** a docstring-only fix. There is no behavior to test, so there is no RED step. I fix it and run the documented suite.
- **Important (switch to ROUND_HALF_UP):** I would not make this change. D2 is an owner decision recorded in the plan (2026-11-02): "round half-even, to match the ledger system." The reviewer's reason is only "customers expect half-up", and the reviewer had no view of D2 or the ledger-system constraint. The spec is the binding authority, and D2 is not a scope fence or one of the five stops. So I decide it as a ruling, record it, and keep going. I do not stall on it.

<edit path="rates/card.py">
    '''Round a price to whole cents. A tie goes to the nearest even cent.'''
</edit>

<command>
make test > .sdd/14-rate-card/final-fix-test.log 2>&1; tail -n 15 .sdd/14-rate-card/final-fix-test.log
</command>

If the suite is green, I commit and append the ledger in one call:

<command>
git add rates/card.py && git commit -m "Fix docstring typo in round_price" && cat >> .sdd/14-rate-card/progress.md <<'EOF'
Final review: Minor (docstring typo "neerest") fixed in rates/card.py; docstring-only, no RED step applicable; make test green.
Ruling: Final review, rates/card.py round_price(): kept ROUND_HALF_EVEN, did not switch to ROUND_HALF_UP — plan Decision D2 (owner, 2026-11-02) requires half-even to match the ledger system; the reviewer cited only customer expectation and did not have D2 — if wrong, customer-facing prices differ by one cent on exact half-cent ties, and a one-line change plus tests fixes it.
EOF
</command>

Then I continue with the plan-completion protocol in `references/final-review.md` (re-reading it first) and `finishing-a-development-branch`. I would not merge or push without the partner's go-ahead.

**Message to partner**

> The final review is done. All tasks are complete and `make test` is green.
>
> - **Fixed:** the docstring typo "neerest" → "nearest" in `rates/card.py`.
> - **Not changed, needs your eye:** the reviewer asked for `round_price()` to use ROUND_HALF_UP because "customers expect half-up." I left it as ROUND_HALF_EVEN. Decision D2 (yours, from the plan review on 2026-11-02) requires half-even to match the ledger system, and the reviewer didn't have that context. I recorded this as a ruling in `.sdd/14-rate-card/progress.md`.
> - **What it costs if wrong:** exact half-cent ties would round to the even cent, which can differ by one cent from what customers expect. Switching is a one-line change plus tests.
> - **Your call:** if the customer-facing expectation should override D2, tell me and I'll make the change test-first. If the ledger system and the customer display need different rounding, that is a separate design question.
>
> The branch is ready for the plan-completion gate. I have not merged or pushed anything.
